notes: THE ALVEOLAR VENTILATION EQUATION - a steady-state MASS BALANCE on CO2, which is why this is conservation and not empirical. All the CO2 produced leaves in the alveolar gas, so its fractional concentration is VCO2/V_A and its partial pressure is that times the dry barometric pressure. RESP.ALVEOLAR.K carries the unit conversion and its derivation. || Written against TOTAL ventilation through C so the whole loop is in the units the chemoreflex sources report and the water flux needs. Identical to K*VCO2/V_A by construction. || IT ASSUMES A STEADY STATE, which ADR 0017 decision 2 licenses: PaCO2 re-equilibrates in minutes and the shortest protocol in this repo is six hours. THE MULTIPLIER IS EXACTLY 1.0 BY DEFAULT, because ADR 0019 decision 4 defaults the metabolic arm off, so this relation is unchanged in every existing configuration.

MASS BALANCE ON WATER VAPOUR. Expired gas leaves saturated at body temperature and inspired gas carries whatever the room holds; RESP.H2O.GAS_CONTENT is the difference and its derivation is on that row. 1440 converts minutes to days and 1e6 converts mg to kg, a kg of water being a litre. || THIS IS THE COMPONENT'S ONLY OUTWARD FLUX and the reason it is not an island. It replaces 39 percent of BF.H2O.INSENSIBLE_LOSS - a row that was assumed and cited 'Convention pending primary source' - with a quantity computed from physical constants and a sourced chemoreflex.

THE ALVEOLAR GAS EQUATION. Every O2 molecule taken up is replaced in the alveolus by CO2 in the ratio RER, so alveolar PO2 is the inspired tension less alveolar PCO2 over that ratio. A steady-state mass balance, which is why this is conservation rather than empirical. || P_dry is RESP.ALVEOLAR.K divided by the STPD-to-BTPS factor 1.21030, so SEA LEVEL IS STATED ONCE IN THE LEDGER and cannot drift between the two components that depend on it. || RER IS THE ONLY PLACE THE CO2 AND O2 SIDES MEET, and it is assumed. phenomenon_citation: The Fick principle. Adolf Fick's 1870 statement that the uptake of a substance by an organ equals blood flow times the arteriovenous concentration difference - a CONSERVATION LAW, which is why this class is conservation and not empirical, and the basis of the reference method for cardiac output in humans for a century.
notes: THE FICK RELATION REARRANGED. Fick determines cardiac output from oxygen uptake and the arteriovenous difference; here cardiac output is already an output of the pressure loop and oxygen uptake is set by metabolism, so the same identity determines the difference. || THE UNIT CHAIN IS THE PART THAT WOULD SILENTLY GO WRONG, as it is for DO2 above: cardiac output is carried in L/DAY because the model's time base is days, oxygen consumption is conventionally per minute, and content is per dL. The 1440 is not decorative.

Mixed venous oxygen content is arterial content less what the tissues took. Definitional given the Fick relation above. || IT IS A WHOLE-BODY MIXED VENOUS VALUE and the model has one systemic compartment, so it represents no particular vein. Regional differences - coronary sinus near 30 percent saturation against renal venous near 90 - are outside this model entirely, and any comparison against a sampled vein other than the pulmonary artery is a category error.

Saturation is the bound oxygen over the carrying capacity. || THE DISSOLVED TERM IS OMITTED HERE WHERE THE ARTERIAL CONTENT INCLUDES IT, which overstates mixed venous saturation by about 0.6 percentage points at rest. That is smaller than the alveolar-arterial difference's own uncertainty and far smaller than the spread of any measurement of this quantity. Including it needs the INVERSE dissociation curve - four more coefficients taken whole from Severinghaus - for a correction below the noise, and the trade is recorded rather than taken silently. || NO HUMAN TARGET IS ASSERTED AGAINST IT, and the reason is an ethical ceiling rather than a gap in the search: mixed venous saturation requires a pulmonary artery catheter, which is not placed in healthy people, so the literature is almost entirely critical care and cardiac disease. Directive 1.7 disqualifies it. Same argument as RN.AUTOREG.UPPER's rat provenance.

The oxygen extraction ratio, identically VO2/DO2 once the unit chains cancel. Written the short way because writing it the long way is a second chance to get the 1440 wrong. || IT IS THE QUANTITY THAT MAKES ANAEMIA LEGIBLE in this model: haemoglobin falls, arterial content and delivery fall with it, consumption does not, so extraction rises. The model has no compensatory rise in cardiac output - ADR 0018 records that omission deliberately - so the extraction ratio here is the WHOLE of the response and therefore an upper bound on it.
